scope: Local MySQL ERD databases and local read-only phpMyAdmin; no application API or production infrastructure

findings.before: Application, backup and migration accounts retained privileges on the obsolete PRD database.
findings.repair: Removed legacy schema/table/column grants and scoped service accounts to the two ERD databases.

findings.before: phpMyAdmin viewer had no failed-login lock policy.
findings.repair: Configured five failed attempts, one-day account lock, TLS and five concurrent connections; persisted in setup code.

findings.summary: ERD-only schema does not validate financial arithmetic/sign/quantity.
evidence: Negative service total accepted by ERD-only schema
Negative sale price accepted by ERD-only schema
Sale total can differ from subtotal and discount
findings.remediation: Add approved column CHECKs and backend validation/transaction rules after business review; keep the 7+5 table model unchanged.

findings.summary: A compromised application SQL credential can bypass session FK checks.
findings.evidence: Confirmed on a clone with the actual runtime principal, then rolled back.
findings.remediation: Keep SQL credentials in backend only; parameterize queries, forbid arbitrary SQL APIs, protect the OS and rotate credentials if exposed. Full mitigation requires a reviewed write API/stored-procedure privilege model.

findings.summary: Backup recovery works, but backups share the local disk and are not encrypted.
findings.evidence: SQL backups restored and compared successfully; ACL protection does not protect against disk theft or disk failure.
findings.remediation: Before real customer data: encrypt backups, keep a separate off-device copy, define retention/scheduling and repeat restore drills. Store encryption keys separately.

findings.before: Configuration path suffixes, repeated slashes and Windows NTFS ADS bypassed the deny rule. The ADS alias served the small config wrapper source, exposing a local include path.
findings.repair: Reject Windows path aliases, repeated leading slashes, double encodings and every config.inc.php suffix before PHP/static routing. The wrapper contains no SQL password; no SQL credential disclosure was observed.

findings.before: Managed CLI helpers verified the CA but did not require the certificate hostname.
findings.repair: Persist VERIFY_IDENTITY after the loopback SAN certificate has been installed.

findings.summary: Foreign keys do not enforce mandatory child/payment presence.
findings.evidence: A service note with no details or payment and a sale with its payment deleted were accepted on test clones.
findings.remediation: Enforce creation/deletion through backend transactions and authorization; approve any further SQL enforcement before modifying the ERD implementation.

findings.before: phpMyAdmin signon defaults removed HttpOnly from the signon session cookie.
findings.repair: Explicit SignonCookieParams preserve HttpOnly and SameSite Strict after phpMyAdmin opens the signon session.
verified_by: Session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite Strict

findings.before: phpMyAdmin overwrote the local no-referrer policy with same-origin.
findings.repair: Apply the local privacy headers through header_register_callback after phpMyAdmin builds its headers.

limits: Case counts include parameterized checks for individual columns/tables; they are not independent exploit families.
Active tables were empty. Recovery was tested for actual empty backups and populated disposable fixtures.
All test writes used scratch schemas/accounts. Production schemas, existing data, draw.io and frontend were preserved.
No whole-application SQL injection, XSS, business authorization, payment gateway or production penetration test: the API is not implemented.
OS-wide listener visibility was incomplete in this execution environment. MySQL reports loopback binding and expected local connections succeed; remote reachability was not independently tested.
No stress/availability attack, exhaustive fuzzing, binary exploit attempt, external scanning or proof of absence of vulnerabilities.
No absolute security guarantee or approval for production use.
